_comment: 4ColThems manifest — the kit's source of truth for theme IDENTITY: which themes exist, in what cycle order, and the handful of facts about each one that live outside CSS (the button label and icon, the mobile chrome colour, the color-scheme, the cldBar/remdev slug). Colour VALUES live in css/themes.css; terminal palettes live in terminal-themes.json. Every other file in the kit mirrors this one (the JS maps, theme4col.py, the CSS blocks) because each has to stand alone once copied into an app — there is no build step joining them. The suite in tests/ is what keeps the mirrors honest: change a theme here, run the tests, and they name every file still out of step.

dark.label: Dark Modern
dark.description: Neutral dark with a blue accent. The default: the bare :root selector carries it, so a page with no data-theme attribute still looks right.

light.label: Light Modern
light.description: The only light theme, and the one that exposes integration bugs: an opaque embed canvas or a wrong color-scheme is invisible on the dark three.

hc.label: Dark High Contrast
hc.source: VS Code 1.118.1 theme-defaults — Dark High Contrast
hc.description: Pure black surfaces; structure is drawn with #6fc3df borders and state with the #f38518 orange. Selection and active states are outlines, not fills.

green.label: Garage Green
green.description: Dark green-tinted phosphor terminal skin with a #36c97a accent and cyan for informational state.
